title: AMD Instinct emerges as second vendor for open RL post-training by H1 2027
body: On July 10 the vLLM project announced that vime - its reinforcement-learning post-training framework - now runs end-to-end on AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs through native ROCm support, a port contributed by AMD engineers and shipped as a prebuilt Docker container that removes the from-source build long gating ROCm adoption. The validated runs matter more than the port itself: on Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and the Qwen3-30B-A3B mixture-of-experts model, throughput held near 4,100 tokens per GPU per second, the training-versus-rollout log-probability divergence stayed around 0.012, and reward climbed from roughly zero to about 0.5-0.6 by step 100 - precisely the numerical-stability and convergence signals a lab inspects before trusting non-NVIDIA silicon for post-training. Reinforcement-learning post-training, not pre-training, is where most of this year's frontier gains are being extracted, and that stage has been almost entirely CUDA-bound, so a working MI355X path hands open-model builders their first credible second hardware vendor for their most compute-hungry phase. The July 10 release is AMD-authored, though, so the real test of whether CUDA's grip on the RL stage is loosening is external validation. I expect that by H1 2027 at least one group independent of AMD and the vime core team publishes an end-to-end open-model RL post-training run on AMD Instinct - or an open-weight model ships whose post-training recipe names AMD Instinct - turning a vendor demo into a reproduced, second-source capability, with AMD's July 22-23 Advancing AI event and the expected MI450 accelerator adding near-term momentum.

reasoning.because: vLLM's vime RL post-training framework now runs end-to-end on AMD Instinct MI355X via native ROCm
reasoning.given: RL post-training drives this year's frontier gains and has been almost entirely CUDA-bound
reasoning.so_that: A group independent of AMD publishes an end-to-end open-model RL post-training run on AMD Instinct
reasoning.landing: by H1 2027; >=1 non-AMD group or open-weight release validates AMD Instinct
reasoning.plain_language: Teaching AIs by trial and error has mostly needed Nvidia chips; AMD just proved it works on theirs, so others will copy it soon.

summary: vLLM's July 10 port put its vime RL post-training framework on AMD Instinct MI355X with native ROCm and validated Qwen3 runs. Since RL post-training drives this year's gains yet stays CUDA-bound, expect a group independent of AMD to publish an open-model RL run on AMD Instinct by H1 2027.
